material_conditions: Precisely define angle, circle, perpendicular and parallel lines, and line segment using undefined point, line, distance along a line and distance around a circular arc.

Represent plane transformations using transparencies or geometric software; model transformations as point-input/output functions; distinguish distance/angle-preserving from nonpreserving transformations (translation vs horizontal stretch).
For a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid or regular polygon, describe rotations/reflections mapping each figure onto itself.
Define rotations, reflections and translations using angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines and line segments.
Draw image of figure under rotation, reflection or translation using graph/tracing/software; specify a sequence of transformations taking one figure onto another.
Use descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures/predict effects and determine congruence of two figures using rigid-motion definition.
Course bracket: use rigid motions as familiar entry to geometric-proof concepts.
Show triangle congruence under rigid motions if and only if corresponding sides AND corresponding angles are congruent; preserve both implications.
Explain how ASA, SAS and SSS triangle-congruence criteria follow from congruence by rigid motions; not rule memorization alone.
